faq_items.question: How do I organize my garage on a budget?
faq_items.answer: Start by purging what you don't use, which is free, then buy clear stackable bins, a roll of labels, and a few wall hooks. Add a secondhand shelving unit rather than pricey branded cabinets. Prioritize getting items off the floor first; structure matters far more than name-brand storage.

faq_items.question: What is the best way to store tools in a garage?
faq_items.answer: Store tools vertically to keep them visible and reachable. Hang hand tools on a wall-mounted pegboard, keep power tools and hardware in a workbench with drawers, and group everything in one dedicated tool zone. Labeling each spot means tools go back where they belong instead of vanishing into bins.

faq_items.question: How do you organize a two-car garage so you can still park?
faq_items.answer: Push storage up and out. Move everything you can lift onto walls and ceiling racks, reserve the floor for wheeled or oversized items, and keep at least a car-width path clear down the center. A six-zone plan along the walls leaves the middle open so the car slides right in.

faq_items.question: What should you not store in a garage?
faq_items.answer: Avoid storing anything sensitive to temperature swings or moisture: paint, propane, paper documents, canned food, medications, and electronics can all degrade or become hazards in an unheated garage. Firewood attracts pests indoors, too. Keep those items inside the house and reserve the garage for tools, gear, and weatherproof supplies.

faq_items.question: How long does it take to organize a garage?
faq_items.answer: Plan for one focused session per zone rather than a single marathon. Most garages take a weekend or two of a few hours each, working zone by zone. Tackling one area at a time, clear, sort, install storage, stop, gets the job finished without the all-at-once burnout.
